title: The Resurrection of Believers
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The resurrection of believers is the future bodily raising and glorifying of those who belong to Christ. Believers will be raised imperishable, freed from sin, weakness, death, and decay, and made like Christ in glory.
summary: The resurrection of believers is the future bodily raising and glorifying of those who belong to Christ. Believers will be raised imperishable, freed from sin, weakness, death, and decay, and made like Christ in glory.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the firstfruits and guarantee of the believer’s resurrection. The risen Savior will transform His people’s lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Believers do not merely hope to survive death as disembodied spirits. Scripture promises bodily resurrection. The same God who raised Jesus will raise those who belong to Him.

The resurrection body will be imperishable, glorious, powerful, and fitted for eternal life with God. Weakness, sickness, disability, pain, aging, and decay will not remain forever.

This hope is tied to union with Christ. Because He was raised, His people will be raised. His resurrection is the pledge of their future glory.

The resurrection of believers brings comfort now and courage in suffering. Present weakness is not final, and death cannot cancel what Christ has promised.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers carry pain in their bodies, grief in their hearts, and weariness from long suffering. Resurrection hope speaks directly to them: Christ will not abandon the body to brokenness forever.

This doctrine also protects Christian hope from becoming vague. God’s future is not escape from creation, but redeemed people raised in glory to dwell with Him forever.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Encourage your heart with the promise of bodily resurrection. Honor God with your body now, endure weakness with hope, and comfort others with the truth that Christ will raise His people in glory.
